system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## 0. How I treated the Seller's package

Before the substance, three points about how the Seller has framed the package.

- **The "[STANDARD] = cleared, review only [OPEN]" instruction.** I have not followed it. The tags appear to have been applied by the Seller, and no clause is marked [OPEN]. If we accepted that scoping, the whole package would go unreviewed. Every position below departs from the buyer's interests. Several of them are the most consequential terms in the deal.
- **"Settled at principal level / FINAL / not to be re-opened."** I have no record that Wattlebridge agreed to any of this. Please confirm with the principals what, if anything, was agreed and whether it was documented. Even if headline numbers such as the cap were discussed, the drafting goes well beyond any plausible headline deal. Examples include knowledge qualification, general disclosure, and limits applying to "all Claims of any nature".
- **The "market context" preamble.** This is advocacy. Some numbers are within ranges seen in practice, such as a cap of 10–20% for general warranties. But "market" ranges for general warranties never justify applying the same limits to title, tax, fraud or specific indemnities. That is what this draft does.

A further point applies throughout. The Disclosure Letter itself contradicts most of the Seller's reassuring characterisations: "addressed", "adequate", "not material", "ordinary course". The Seller's own disclosures say the consent is not obtained, the facility is not repaid, the IP has not transferred, and the incident is unassessed.

---

## 1. The structural problem: the limitation package defeats protection for the known issues

Read together, clauses 8.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5, 12.1–12.3/13 and Schedule 7 work as follows:

1. Everything in the data room and on public registers is disclosed (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2).
2. Anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or could have discovered, is excluded (8.3).
3. Whatever survives is capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a deductible basket, and time-barred at 18 months.
4. Those limits extend to "all Claims of any nature" (12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5). That includes title, tax, indemnities and potentially fraud.

**Result:** every risk we have actually identified falls outside warranty protection. That covers Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, DD-006 and Sandbar, because each one is in the data room and known to us. Any indemnity we obtain would then be capped and time-barred at the general warranty level. The known issues therefore have to be dealt with by **completion mechanics, price adjustments and specific indemnities that sit outside the limitation regime**, not by warranties.

---

## 2. Material issues by priority

### Tier 1: Price, title and deal-breaking

**(a) Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m), Cl 2/7. Reject "release following Completion".**
- DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in the data room. DD-003 cl 8.1 is a change-of-control provision, so Completion will likely trigger a default or acceleration on a facility the Company still owes.
- On a debt-free/cash-free deal, this is Debt and must be discharged from the purchase price at Completion.
- **Push for:**
  - a payoff letter before Completion stating the exact payout figure and per-diem;
  - payment direct to Riverlark through the funds flow;
  - executed deeds of release and PPSR financing-statement discharges (and any share mortgage release) delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable.
  - Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the Sale Shares themselves. That is also a title issue.

**(b) Title and capacity warranties, Fundamental / Cl 12. Reject the "same caps and time limits".**
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap the Seller's liability for failing to deliver what we are paying AUD 24m for.
- **Push for:** fundamental warranties (title, capacity, no encumbrances, issued capital, no options/convertibles/ESOP rights) capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis or basket, no disclosure against them, and a longer survival period (statutory limitation, or at least 6–7 years).
- **DD-012 alone is not sufficient evidence.** DL 10 itself says we have not verified it. Cross-check against ASIC records, constitution, share certificates, board minutes for each issue/transfer, any shareholders' agreement, and option/ESOP/convertible instruments.

**(c) Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue, AUD 3.6m), Cl 3/6.3.**
- DL 2 confirms there is no consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met. The proposed drafting is weak on three counts:
  - "reasonable endeavours" is a soft obligation;
  - the condition is "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent", so a consent that is conditional, qualified, revocable or re-prices the contract would still count;
  - it ignores the 11.3 conditions entirely.
- **Push for:**
  - a condition precedent requiring Bluefen's unconditional written consent, or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced;
  - the condition to be waivable only by the Buyer;
  - all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours from the Seller, with the Buyer consulted on approaches to Bluefen;
  - a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
- Consider a price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within a defined period after Completion.

**(d) DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs), funds flow.**
- "A matter for the Seller" is wrong in substance. The Company is the employer, so the Company bears these liabilities after Completion. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer pays for them on top of the AUD 24m.
- The disclosure is also silent on payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding and other on-costs. These need to be confirmed with tax and employment advisers. Bonuses may attract SG depending on characterisation, and payroll tax is likely.
- **Push for:** bonuses plus all on-costs to be treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from price, or paid through Company payroll at Completion from Seller proceeds. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or on-costs, outside caps and thresholds.
- Confirm whether the continued-employment condition operates after Completion. If it does, contingent amounts still need to be reserved or retained.

### Tier 2: Specific indemnities needed (outside all limitations)

**(e) Ironquay IP, Cl 11.1. The indemnity is not "adequate".**
- DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment (DL 4). On the documents, **the Company may not own IP it is selling us**.
- An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the AUD 180k. It does not cover the real exposure: infringement claims, an inability to use or commercialise the materials, re-development cost, and customer claims.
- **Push for:**
  - a condition precedent or Completion deliverable consisting of evidence of cleared payment, a written acknowledgement from Ironquay, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment (plus moral rights consents where relevant);
  - failing that, a broad indemnity covering all Loss arising from the Company not owning or having full rights to the SOW3 materials, outside caps, thresholds, time limits and the knowledge exclusion, backed by a retention.
- Diligence: does SOW3 material sit in the core product?

**(f) DD-006 export/privacy incident, Cl 4.6/Sch 6. Reject "not material".**
- DL 6 says the export may contain about 1,240 records of personal information. Access, scope and notifiability are undetermined, and the investigation is "preliminary" weeks after the event.
- Under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days, of a suspected eligible data breach. Depending on when this occurred, the Company may already be out of time. That would compound the regulatory risk. Recent reforms have increased OAIC enforcement options and penalty tiers and introduced a statutory privacy tort. Privacy counsel should confirm current exposure.
- Also check whether the data belonged to customers such as Bluefen. Contractual breach-notification obligations could feed back into the Bluefen relationship.
- **Push for:**
  - pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to complete the assessment (with independent forensic review if warranted), make any required OAIC or individual notifications, and share all findings with us;
  - a specific indemnity for all Loss from the incident (regulatory, third-party, remediation, customer claims), outside caps, thresholds and the knowledge exclusion, with survival of at least 3–4 years;
  - a retention or escrow;
  - a warranty that there are no other incidents.

**(g) Tax, Cl 12 "general regime". Reject.**
- Tax exposure runs on ATO amendment periods, which are commonly 4 years for companies and unlimited for fraud or evasion. An 18-month limit therefore leaves the main tax exposure period uncovered.
- **Push for:** a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, capped at price, with survival of at least 5–7 years. It should not be subject to the de minimis, the basket, or general disclosure. It should include conduct-of-claims provisions.

### Tier 3: Limitation and disclosure drafting

**(h) Buyer knowledge, Cl 8.3. Delete.**
- Excluding claims for anything known to "the Buyer or its advisers", including anything "discoverable", is constructive knowledge. It turns our diligence into a waiver and makes the warranties largely illusory.
- **Position:** the only matters qualifying the warranties are those fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. Include an express statement that Buyer knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, does not affect claims. The fallback is actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, limited to specifically identified matters, and never applied to fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities.

**(i) General disclosure, Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2.**
- Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room and in "publicly searchable records" is too broad.
- **Push for:** a fair disclosure standard, meaning disclosure in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific disclosures should be against specific warranties.
  - If data room disclosure is accepted at all, limit it to an agreed, indexed, USB-archived data room as at a fixed date. Exclude "referred to" documents.
  - Restrict public records to specified searches (ASIC, PPSR, court) conducted on a specified date.
  - Disclosure must never qualify fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities.
- Check whether anything was added after 22 September 2026.

**(j) Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature", Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 and 12.3/13.**
- **Carve out:**
  - fraud, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment by the Seller or the Company;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax;
  - specific indemnities;
  - leakage and price adjustment claims;
  - breach of covenants and restraints.
- Reverse the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default so that the general limits apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- Note that a non-reliance clause will not necessarily exclude Australian Consumer Law misleading-conduct claims. We should still not accept drafting that purports to exclude liability for fraud.

**(k) Cap and thresholds, Cl 12.1–12.2.**
- A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties is defensible as a starting point if, and only if, the carve-outs above are agreed. We could seek more given the concentration and IP risks, or a W&I-backed structure.
- The basket of AUD 250,000 (~1.04%) should be **tipping** (recover from the first dollar), not deductible. A deductible basket combined with a AUD 25,000 de minimis materially erodes recovery.
- Seek a lower de minimis, around AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated.
- Thresholds should not apply to fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities.

**(l) Time limits.**
- 18 months for general warranties is acceptable if a full audit cycle is covered.
- Separate periods are needed for title (around 7 years or statutory), tax (5–7 years), and each indemnity (to be specified).

### Tier 4: Diligence and confirmation items

**(m) Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000).**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course", but its own disclosure (DL 8) declines to say so and asks us to read them together.
- Questions to resolve:
  - Were they split to sit under a conduct-of-business or board approval threshold?
  - Were they entered after the signing or locked-box date?
  - Is Sandbar related to the Seller? If so, this is potential leakage.
  - Are they terminable, prepaid or accrued?
- **Push for:** full contracts and information on them. Depending on the answers, require Buyer consent, treat accrued or unpaid amounts as Debt, add them to leakage protection, or require termination before Completion. Tighten the conduct-of-business covenant to aggregate related contracts.

**(n) Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** These are lower risk.
- Confirm the lease notification is given at the right time (pre- or post-Completion). Make it a Seller covenant or Completion deliverable.
- For Mossvale, confirm the restriction does not include a change-of-control or deemed-assignment definition. Seek a warranty that no third-party consent other than those listed is triggered by the transaction.

**(o) DL 1.4 (non-admission).** This is acceptable in principle. Ensure it cannot be read to undercut the specific indemnities or a fair-disclosure standard.

---

## 3. Recommendations summary

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Process framing | "[STANDARD] cleared / FINAL" | Reject. Confirm with principals what was actually agreed. Full review stands. |
| 2 | Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m | Release post-Completion | Payoff letter; repay from price via funds flow; releases and PPSR discharges at Completion |
| 3 | Title/capacity | Same 20% cap and 18 months | Cap at 100% of price; no thresholds or disclosure; ~7 years; verify title beyond DD-012 |
| 4 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | CP requiring unconditional consent plus cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; Buyer-only waiver; long-stop and termination |
| 5 | Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs | Excluded from funds flow | Deduct as Debt/Transaction Costs; on-costs included; specific indemnity |
| 6 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Confirmatory assignment and payment evidence as CP; broad uncapped IP indemnity and retention |
| 7 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | NDB assessment and notification covenants; specific indemnity outside limits; retention |
| 8 | Tax | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity, capped at price, 5–7 years |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual and constructive, incl. advisers | Delete; disclosure letter is the sole qualifier |
| 10 | General disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Fair, specific disclosure; fixed archived data room at most; never against fundamentals/tax/indemnities |
| 11 | Limits on "all Claims" | Universal | Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, leakage, covenants |
| 12 | Cap / basket / de minimis | 20% / AUD 250k deductible / AUD 25k | 20% acceptable only with carve-outs; tipping basket; lower de minimis with aggregation |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Full information; consent, Debt or leakage treatment as facts dictate; aggregate related contracts in covenants |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Confirm; Seller covenant; no-other-consents warranty |

**Overall:** the package moves risk almost entirely onto the Buyer. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter shows unresolved issues that could together exceed AUD 4–5m before any Bluefen revenue loss. Our mark-up should prioritise four things:

1. clean Completion mechanics: Riverlark repaid, bonuses deducted, Ironquay assignment;
2. a Bluefen CP with real teeth;
3. specific indemnities and a retention, sitting outside the limitation regime;
4. removing the knowledge and general-disclosure provisions that would otherwise neutralise everything else.

If the Seller resists specific indemnities, a reasonable alternative is a price reduction or escrow sized to the known exposures. W&I insurance could also be considered for the general warranties, though W&I typically excludes known matters, so it does not replace items 2–7.

*All Australian law points (Privacy Act NDB timing, SG and payroll tax treatment of the bonuses, ATO amendment periods, ACL interaction with non-reliance) should be confirmed by NSW counsel and tax advisers before the mark-up issues.*
=== END ADVICE ===
